title: Does the reduction split when the index halves (frozen side check)
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, frozen before any run (sub-goal B91's first step). At every eigenvalue with even k = 2c >= 4 for sides 16, 32 and 64: the reduction M of the family to ker X_b with the monomial complement W_0 and with a complement W' containing k G Y^j (2j < k - 1), each in two parametrizations (Zhat in l = u/(1 + u), and Z(a + au)/(1 + u) in u). Test S1: every entry (i, j) with i + j odd vanishes modulo the parameter to the power 2k; test S2: every entry with i + j even has only odd powers of the parameter below 2k. B91's strong form predicts S1 and S2 for at least one of the four variants at every tested eigenvalue. Decision rule: if a variant passes everywhere, the epic considers the induction on k and says which route it takes and why; otherwise B91's strong form is recorded as refuted, the halving of the leading matrix (CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001A, Theorem 3) stands, and the epic proceeds with ticket A. Disclosed: at k = 6, side 32, a = alpha^23, the W_0 entry (0, 1) has valuation 10 < 12, so S1 already fails for W_0 there (valuations do not depend on the parametrization).
failure_conditions: Some variant passes S1 and S2 at every tested eigenvalue (then B91's strong form stands at these sides), or every variant fails somewhere (then it is refuted at these sides).
remaining_obligations: the frozen test and its decision
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10 (sub-goals B73 and B91).
